title: Normalized derived direct-image slice comparison and invertibility of its mate
statement: Let $\mathcal D$ and $\mathcal C$ be small categories with Grothendieck topologies $K$ and $J$, let $u:\mathcal D\to\mathcal C$ be continuous, let $R$ and $S$ be sheaves of commutative rings on them, and let $a:R\to u_*S$ be a sheaf ring map. Suppose $u^{-1}$ on sheaves of sets preserves finite limits. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] with chosen localization universes. For a continuous morphism of small ringed sites with left exact inverse image, fix an object V, its localized morphism, and any normalized global and localized derived adjunction presentations [def-weil-pbc-ringed-slice-derived-data]. There is a natural isomorphism beta from restriction after derived direct image to local derived direct image after restriction, whose square with the right-derived units and the termwise restriction factorizations commutes on every complex. Its inverse adjunction mate is invertible. No section localization assertion is part of this lemma.

proof.text: 1. Use the generic K-injective derivability structure for the composite of ordinary pushforward and restriction. The unit for derived pushforward followed by derived restriction is invertible on K-injectives. Restriction preserves K-injectives, so the comparison unit for restriction followed by the local right derived pushforward is also invertible on K-injectives. The good-object criterion proves that both composites are right derived functors of the same ordinary composite. Right-derived uniqueness gives beta. Its factorization equation, conjugated by the two restriction factorizations, gives the displayed normalization on every complex. 2. Apply the inverse-mate invertibility lemma to this normalized beta.

proof_origin.place: K-injective derivability, rightDerivedUnique and its factorization equation, followed by the inverse-mate lemma.
